chapter: Dave and Iola: faith and values
title: 'La Fiesta de la Posada' and Chris's 'Mary Magdalene and the Garden Dweller'
summary: Chris describes performing the Posada with choruses, a donkey mishap, and a new piece about Mary Magdalene in Dave's style.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Dan and I have often played that piece with our dad called “La Fiesta de la Posada.” And it usually would happen in December, these performances. And God, Christmas has gotten so just pukingly commercialized. I was trying to think of a worse word than disgustingly and I came up with that one. I don’t know if it’s a real word. But you would get the real sense of Christmas and love when you do this piece, “La Fiesta de la Posada” ‘cause it has a chorus, which is usually like town folk that like singing you know. And that’s a whole different thing. You know it’s almost Communistic. It’s not professional singers usually, it’s just people that love singing, it’s an expression of their spirit. And if there’s a children’s choir in it, and there’s a Mary and there’s three wise men. I mean we’ve done it in Durango, Colorado where they had Mary — they had a live donkey bringing Mary in.

Yeah well the donkey relieved himself on the way up to the stage. And you know the three wise men, you know it’s funny ‘cause like if you just put on your funny hat, they’ve got sombreros, it looks like the Three Amigos. But it’s in the reflective of the real tradition of “La Fiesta de la Posada” is about, it’s amazing what survived in the Bible, that you have you know Joseph and Mary, they’re not rich, they’re really poor, they’re refugees. That’s all set up, you know at least we have an open heart and kindness. Who knows what’s going to come out of a refugee? I mean look at Obama in a way. Well not that his parents were refugees but —
He was born in a different country though. We all know that.

No, but I mean he didn’t come from a classic mother-father “Leave it to Beaver” background. It’s like just that that potential is all there. And I just wrote a piece that Dan and Darius played on their premier called “Mary Magdalene and the Garden Dweller” and I was hired specifically to write a piece in the style of Dave with jazz and also chorus and orchestra. And one of the things that amazes me is if you look at how nuns don’t have the powers of priests, and you know the church has always been so patriarchal. But it’s amazing that despite all that and despite all these filthy old bishops and abbots and probably popes that wanted to white-wash it, that Mary Magdalene is this powerful person who had more courage than all the disciples. When they’re all quivering in their boots hiding in an attic she’s the one that sees Jesus as a garden dweller and says, “Listen you chicken shits, get out there and spread the Gospel.” And it’s amazing that that part has survived. How did that happen with all this? And maybe that part’s divine that despite all — there must have been a huge conspiracy to get rid of that stuff. That empowered women you know. But it’s there still in the Bible.
